advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make `_check_wrapper_call` position-aware (reuse `_git_subcommand`) so a mutation-verb word appearing as a non-subcommand argument does not fire `wrapper-git-mutation`.
evidence: `verb = next((t for t in tokens if t in MUTATION_VERBS), None)` (scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py:360)
Contrast the raw path which is position-aware: `sub = _git_subcommand(tokens)` then `elif isinstance(sub, str) and sub in MUTATION_VERBS:` (scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py:332-336)

MUTATION_VERBS includes generic words like `reset`, `add`, `clean`, `mv` that legitimately appear as ref names / patterns / message words: `MUTATION_VERBS = frozenset({"add", "commit", "rm", "mv", "reset", "update-ref", "checkout", "clean"})` (scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py:44-46)
advisory.finding: `_check_wrapper_call` detects a mutation verb by scanning ALL token arguments (`next((t for t in tokens if t in MUTATION_VERBS))`) without checking the git SUBCOMMAND position, unlike the raw-subprocess path which uses `_git_subcommand`. A benign read through a wrapper name that passes a mutation-verb *word* as a non-subcommand argument (e.g. a ref/branch named `reset`, a `--grep reset` pattern, or a commit-message token) will be flagged as `wrapper-git-mutation`, a false positive requiring a spurious marker.
scenarios: `run_git(cwd, "rev-parse", "add")` or a branch/ref literally named a mutation verb
advisory.suggested_fix: After assembling `tokens`, resolve the subcommand with `_git_subcommand(tokens)` (skipping a leading tracker/cwd operand as appropriate) and only emit when that resolved subcommand is in MUTATION_VERBS, matching the raw-subprocess path.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Track each run block's true starting line (e.g. from the YAML node/line mapping) instead of first-occurrence substring matching so Layer W line numbers are correct.
evidence: `_first_line_of` returns the first match anywhere in the file: `for i, line in enumerate(text_lines, start=1): if target in line: return i` (scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py:557-559)

27 workflow run blocks begin with the same `set -euo pipefail` line (search_files: reconcile-bridge.yml:98,113,124,134,165,196,215,227,284,413 and others), so every such step collapses to the first occurrence's line number
advisory.finding: Layer W hit/violation line numbers are computed from `_first_line_of`, which returns the FIRST file-wide line that contains the run block's first line. Because many workflow run blocks begin with the identical `set -euo pipefail`, `base_line` (and therefore every `base_line + offset` hit line) is attributed to the wrong step, misreporting the location of a real violation.
scenarios: An unsanctioned `git add` in the reconcile-bridge commit-back step (~line 291) reported at the first `set -euo pipefail` occurrence (~line 98)
advisory.suggested_fix: Use a line-tracking YAML loader (e.g. a SafeLoader subclass capturing node.start_mark.line) to get each step's real run-block start line rather than `_first_line_of`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Restrict marker detection to actual Python comment tokens (e.g. via tokenize) rather than substring-searching raw source lines.
evidence: `m = _MARKER_RE.search(line)` over plain text lines (scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py:138-139), not comment tokens

EXCLUDED_FILES exists specifically because the test module embeds marker text as fixtures: `Path("tests/unit/test_raw_git_write_lint.py")` (scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py:83-86) and the module docstring notes 'the test module itself contains raw-write shapes as string fixtures'
advisory.finding: `_MARKER_RE` is searched against raw source lines, so a `# raw-git-ok:` sequence appearing inside a string literal or docstring is treated as a real sanction marker (or, if reason-empty, a `marker-without-reason` violation). This is only mitigated by hard-coding the lint's own test file into EXCLUDED_FILES; any future src/scripts file containing that literal text would get a spurious sanction or violation.
scenarios: A src file whose docstring or an error string mentions `# raw-git-ok:` to document the convention

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Report `marker-without-reason` in shell/workflow blocks at the marker's real line (base_line + its index).
evidence: `Violation(rel, base_line, "marker-without-reason", ...)` for `_ in empty_markers` (scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py:503-509) — uses base_line, discarding the per-marker line index
The violation list is built before `if not _block_has_tracker_context(...): return [], violations` (scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py:510-511)
advisory.finding: In `_scan_shell_block`, an empty `# raw-git-ok:` marker anywhere in a run/shell block emits a `marker-without-reason` violation at `base_line` (the block's first line) rather than the marker's actual line, and it is emitted before the tracker-context gate, so it fires even for blocks that are otherwise entirely out of scope.
scenarios: An empty marker on line N of a multi-line workflow step reported at the step's first line

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that runs the lint against the real repo tree (root=REPO_ROOT) and asserts check() returns no violations, pinning the bootstrap-clean invariant.
evidence: search for `check(REPO_ROOT)` / `REPO_ROOT` usage as a scan root in tests/unit/test_raw_git_write_lint.py returned no matches; every test uses the `tree` (tmp_path) fixture
ticket d37e Testing: 'Full-tree run is clean at merge'; AC: 'the tree is clean at landing'
scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py:623 `def check(root: Path)` accepts an arbitrary root but is only ever driven against tmp_path in the suite
search for 'class' in tests/unit/test_raw_git_write_lint.py returned no matches — every fixture uses module- or def-level bodies
scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py:420 `if isinstance(stmt, ast.ClassDef):` spawns a sub-scope linter for class bodies
the diff marks a method: src/rebar/review_bot/gerrit_client.py `def clone_change_ref(self, ...):  # raw-git-ok: disposable sandbox repo, not the tracker`
advisory.finding: The lint's central contract — 'the whole repo tree is clean under the new gate after all 107 bootstrap hits are marked' (ticket AC: 'the tree is clean at landing'; Testing: 'Full-tree run is clean at merge') — is verified only by CI, not by any test. Every test uses synthetic tmp_path trees; none calls check(REPO_ROOT)/main on the actual repo. A malformed or missing `# raw-git-ok:` marker among the 37 sites changed here (e.g. an empty reason, or a mutation site left unmarked) would pass the unit suite and only fail in CI.
merged_from: No test exercises a git mutation or a raw-git-ok marker inside a class method, yet the real diff sanctions a class method (gerrit_client.clone_change_ref) and the linter has a dedicated ClassDef scope branch plus method-level function-marker resolution. A regression in class-body traversal (mutations inside methods not detected, or method markers not honored) would be regression-blind.
scenarios: A future edit adds a raw git mutation without a marker, or an author writes `# raw-git-ok:` with an empty reason on a real seam
One of the 37 markers in this diff is on the wrong line (function marker not matching def/first-body/line-above) so the hit stays unsanctioned
advisory.suggested_fix: Add `def test_real_tree_is_clean(lint): assert lint.check(REPO_ROOT) == []` (mirroring how the marker disposition is meant to hold at landing).

evidence: scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py:333-334 `sub = _git_subcommand(tokens); if sub is _OPAQUE: self._emit(call, 'unresolvable-argv', 'git argv subcommand position is not a literal')`
search for 'subcommand position is not a literal' across tests returned no matches — only the source line
existing opaque tests (test_opaque_raw_subprocess_fires_fail_closed) cover a bare-argv Name, not a resolved-list-with-nonliteral-subcommand
advisory.finding: The 'git argv subcommand position is not a literal' opaque branch is untested: a raw subprocess whose git subcommand token is a variable (e.g. `subprocess.run(['git','-C',t,verb])`) should emit `unresolvable-argv` via _git_subcommand returning _OPAQUE, but no test exercises this path.
scenarios: A bypass author writes `git -C tracker <verb>` where verb is computed, expecting it to slip past a literal-only matcher
